16 English mistakes Spanish speakers make

Most mistakes Spanish speakers make in English are Spanish grammar carried across word for word. Here are the 16 we see most, each with the wrong sentence, the right one, and the Spanish pattern behind it.

Last updated 11 November 2026

  1. Age with "have"
  2. "Have" for feelings
  3. "Be agree"
  4. "People is"
  5. Missing subject
  6. "Depend of"
  7. "Explain me" / "say me"
  8. "For" + verb
  9. "The last week"
  10. "More better"
  11. "Do a mistake"
  12. "Married with"
  13. "Want that you"
  14. Double negative
  15. Present with "since"
  16. "Like" + plain verb

1. Age with "have"

I have 25 years.I'm 25 years old.

Use "be" for age: "I am 25 years old." Spanish says "tengo 25 años".

2. "Have" for feelings

I have hungry.I'm hungry.

Use "be": "I am hungry", "you are right". Spanish says "tengo hambre".

3. "Be agree"

I am agree with you.I agree with you.

"Agree" is already the verb: "I agree." Spanish says "estoy de acuerdo".

4. "People is"

People is very friendly here.People are very friendly here.

"People" is plural: "people are". "La gente" is singular in Spanish.

5. Missing subject

Is raining today.It's raining today.

English always needs a subject: "It is raining." Spanish can drop it: "está lloviendo".

6. "Depend of"

It depends of the price.It depends on the price.

It is "depend on". Spanish says "depende de".

7. "Explain me" / "say me"

Can you explain me the problem?Can you explain the problem to me?

Say "explain it to me" or "tell me". Spanish says "explícame", "dime".

8. "For" + verb

I came to London for learn English.I came to London to learn English.

Use "to" for a purpose: "to learn English". Spanish says "para aprender".

9. "The last week"

I saw her the last week.I saw her last week.

No "the": "last week", "next year". Spanish says "la semana pasada".

10. "More better"

This one is more better.This one is better.

One comparative is enough: "better", "easier". A copy of "más".

11. "Do a mistake"

I did a mistake.I made a mistake.

These go with "make": "make a mistake". "Hacer" is both do and make.

12. "Married with"

She is married with a doctor.She is married to a doctor.

It is "married to". Spanish says "casado con".

13. "Want that you"

I want that you come.I want you to come.

Say "I want you to come." Spanish says "quiero que vengas".

14. Double negative

I don't know nothing about it.I don't know anything about it.

Use "anything" or "anybody" after "not". Spanish doubles it: "no tengo nada".

15. Present with "since"

I live here since 2020.I've lived here since 2020.

Use "have": "I have lived here since 2020." Spanish uses the present: "vivo aquí desde".

16. "Like" + plain verb

I like play football.I like playing football.

After "like", use -ing: "I like playing football." Spanish says "me gusta jugar".

How to stop making them

Knowing the rule is not enough; the fix has to come out of your mouth without thinking. Say the correct sentence out loud five times, then use it in a real answer. Speech Mode flags these mistakes as you answer, and Fill the Gap drills them one by one.
